solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Section of church's indiscretion left out

indicators.note: out tells us the letter for left is taken away from the slip

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or indiscretion

explanation.surface: Part of a church's story was a scandal that has been hushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' reads as one phrase, but 'left' gives L and 'out' says remove it from LAPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The apse is the vaulted semicircular recess at the east end of a church, so it is a section of one.

clue.text: Superior height? We've taller monkeys!

indicators.note: to monkey with something is to tamper with it, so these letters are messed about

explanation.surface: Primates boast to rivals that they stand taller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monkeys' looks like the subject of the boast but is a verb signalling the anagram of WEVE and TALLER; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful: the level of the water's surface is its height, and water lies above whatever is beneath it, so it is a superior height.

clue.text: Greek characters' super, very big bags

indicators.note: bags here means holds inside, as a bag holds its contents

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
mega is slang for super or excellent

explanation.surface: Greek people with great, enormous luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bags' looks like a noun but is a verb: OS holds MEGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so several of them are Greek characters.

clue.text: Smitten, so denied considering single option

indicators.note: something smitten has been struck hard, so these letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: A lovestruck person, rejected, weighs up having only one choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smitten' suggests being in love, but it is the anagram signal on SO DENIED.
explanation.definitionFit: A biased argument or view looks at just one side, taking only a single possibility into account.

clue.text: Panther's tail caught in trap — show ivories happily with it

indicators.note: caught in says the tail letter sits inside the trap

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for animals

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A panther, its tail snared, still bares its teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivories are teeth (piano keys too). 'with it' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To beam broadly is to smile and show one's teeth, here called ivories, cheerfully.

clue.text: Jet black parts look American

indicators.note: parts says the black letter splits the other two pieces

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Pieces of jet-black American appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet black' reads as a colour, but 'Jet' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Airbus is a European manufacturer whose airliners are jet aircraft.

clue.text: Fantastic pairs the norm in strip club

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or bizarre, so these letters are rearranged extravagantly

explanation.surface: Couples find the usual routine at a striptease venue wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is all fourteen letters of PAIRS THE NORM IN.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a British chain of lap-dancing venues, a well-known brand of strip club.

clue.text: Team almost call in reserve player from the street

indicators.note: in places the team and call pieces inside the reserve word

parts.note: to order something is to reserve or book it
a gang is a team of workers

indicators.note: almost means the call word stops one letter short

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them

explanation.surface: A squad nearly summons a substitute who learnt the game on the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserve player' looks like a substitute, but 'reserve' gives ORDER, which holds GANG and RIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A street musician who cranks a barrel organ is someone playing in the street.

clue.text: Most of spring, they turn hit into trailer for cash

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the spring word is dropped

parts.note: to bound is to spring or leap

indicators.note: hit means struck, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Springtime vandals turn a pop hit into a cash-making advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trailer' suggests a film preview but means someone who trails a quarry; 'into' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tracks down wanted fugitives for a reward follows their trail for money.

clue.text: Hugely exaggerate layer's position?

definitions.meaning: to overdo or overstate something grossly
a layer is a hen, and when brooding she sits on top of her egg

explanation.surface: A hen's spot on the nest, overstated.
explanation.definitionFit: To over-egg the pudding is the idiom for overdoing or overstating; read literally, the two words place a laying hen above her egg.

clue.text: Surveyor's beginning with land that prevents flooding

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: and means with or plus
to bag something is to land or capture it

explanation.surface: A surveyor starts with ground that keeps the floods out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' looks like ground being surveyed but is a verb meaning catch, giving BAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A sack filled with sand is piled up to block rising water and stop it entering.

clue.text: For speech, snitch used space group scheduled, wasting time

parts.note: NASA is the US space agency

indicators.note: wasting means the time letter is thrown away

parts.note: listed means put on a schedule

explanation.surface: An informer's statement about a space agency's planned mission, with time running out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snitch' looks like an informer, but it is slang for the nose: speech produced through the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound is nasalised when air passes through the nose in speaking, so the snitch, or hooter, is used.

clue.text: "Yes, I rowed" mentions Redgrave?

indicators.note: mentions signals that the words quoted contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: An Olympic oarsman confirms his rowing career.
explanation.walkthrough: Steve Redgrave, Britain's five-time Olympic rowing champion, was knighted, so he is a Sir; the answer runs across 'yeS I Rowed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Redgrave is a knight, so his title is the honorific given to knights, an example indicated by the question mark.

clue.text: Ford Scorpio at first using brake for amber?

indicators.note: to ford is to cross through, so the letter passes into the middle of the brake word

parts.note: a rein is a check or brake

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A Ford Scorpio car brakes at an amber traffic light.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Scorpio was a car, but 'Ford' is a verb here: S crosses through REIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is fossilised tree sap, an example of this sticky plant substance, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Place less damp dish on a raw salad?

indicators.note: a salad is a jumble or mixture, so these letters are tossed together

explanation.surface: Putting a damp dish on a raw salad is a poor idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salad' looks like food but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The leeward side of mountains receives little rainfall, so it is a drier area than the windward side.

clue.text: Every drunk essentially loaned capital

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order
essentially takes the central letters, the essence, of the word

explanation.surface: Every drunk basically gets money on loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money but is a city; the middle letters of LOANED are AN.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Armenia.

clue.text: Settlements for surplus Apple scientist accepting work on Sunday

indicators.note: on places the Sunday letter after the rest in an across-style charade
accepting means the scientist takes the work letter inside

parts.note: Isaac Newton is said to have been inspired by a falling apple
W is the symbol for work in physics

explanation.surface: A scientist with surplus apples agrees to work on Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain's postwar new towns were built to house overspill population from crowded cities.
explanation.definitionFit: These planned communities were created to absorb excess population from overcrowded cities.

clue.text: Bum doctor provided session for reduction

parts.note: if means provided that

indicators.note: for reduction says the session word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a term is a session, as at school

explanation.surface: A doctor specialising in bottoms offers a weight-loss session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' looks anatomical but means a vagrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bum is a layabout or tramp, someone who wanders aimlessly from place to place.

clue.text: Zip up new flies covering pair

indicators.note: flies means the new letter departs
up turns the zip word backwards in a down answer

parts.note: nowt is northern English for nothing, as is zip

explanation.surface: Someone fastens new trouser flies over a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zip up' and 'flies' suggest trousers; reversing NOWT gives TWON, then N leaves. 'covering' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is a set of two, so the number is a synonym.

clue.text: Before deal, it nullified shepherds in turn

indicators.note: in turn means the held letters are read backwards
shepherds means herds or encloses, so the clue words hold the letters

explanation.surface: The deal fell through, with sheep-handlers taking it in turns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shepherds' is a verb: the words hold LITNU, which 'in turn' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean up to the time of something, as in waiting till or prior to an event.

clue.text: Well-to-do type receives tips for elite start

indicators.note: receives means the posh word holds the tips inside

parts.note: a toff is a posh, wealthy person

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A rich man takes hints for getting into high society.
explanation.walkthrough: The tips of 'elite' are E and E.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf one begins a round by driving from the tee, so the phrase means to begin.

clue.text: Current returns given by Scotland's banks, individual is putting away rapidly

indicators.note: returns means the current word comes back reversed

parts.note: a flow is a current

indicators.note: the banks of a word are its outer letters, like a river's banks

parts.note: own means individual or particular to oneself

explanation.surface: Currents come back to the riverbanks of Scotland as a person tidies things away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' and 'banks' suggest a river; 'given by' and 'is' are links. Outer letters of 'Scotland' are S and D.
explanation.definitionFit: To wolf food is to bolt or gobble it, eating it greedily and fast.

clue.text: Lightning originally seen by some roof exits

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of the following word

parts.note: eaves are the overhanging lower edge of a roof

explanation.surface: A flash of lightning seen near some rooftop exits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: When someone departs, they go away; the verb is a synonym of exits.

clue.text: Rock band gets in to see effect of repeated bowing

indicators.note: gets in means the band goes inside the to word

parts.note: taken as written
REM was an American rock band
lo is an old word meaning see or behold

explanation.surface: A rock group gains entry to view a show of repeated curtain calls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowing' suggests taking a bow, but it is bowing a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapidly moving a violin bow back and forth on one note produces this trembling musical effect.

clue.text: Monster, so retiring

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, so

explanation.surface: A beast that is, accordingly, shy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like shy but means drawing back.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy-tale giant that eats people is a classic monster.

clue.text: Princely provision — a roast taking forever

parts.note: to pan or roast something is to criticise it harshly
an age is a very long time, seemingly forever

explanation.surface: A royal banquet's joint of meat takes ages to cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roast' looks culinary but means slate; 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An appanage is the land or allowance granted to younger royal children for their upkeep.

clue.text: Falcon working out odds over English spots

indicators.note: over places the first piece above the English letter in this down answer
working out the odd letters means removing them, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A falcon is calculating the odds on spotting English prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working out odds' sounds like calculating chances but removes F, L, O, leaving ACN.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition causing pimples, which are commonly called spots.

clue.text: It helps orienteers pick cycling club opening elsewhere

indicators.note: cycling means the first letter goes round to the end

parts.note: a preference is one's pick or choice

indicators.note: opening elsewhere means the club word's first letter is sent away

parts.note: a joint is a club or nightspot

explanation.surface: Choosing a cycling club that opens somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling club' reads as one phrase, but 'cycling' moves P of PREFERENCE to its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Orienteers navigate by fixed landmarks on a map, marks against which they get their bearings.
